relevance_note: Two individually described patients with SSADH deficiency, one with a printed homozygous ALDH5A1 variant: "a homozygous state for a novel missense mutation (c.667T>C; p.Cys223Arg)".
method_note: Built by a short Python script from my own reading; no table in the paper. Labels: 'patient 1'/'patient 2' (paper's lowercase form, most frequent). Parents of patient 1 are described only as 'his parents' (both sequenced, T/C heterozygotes at c.667), so labelled 'parent of patient 1' and 'parent of patient 1 2'; which is mother/father is not stated. Patient 1 inheritance recorded as 'inherited unspecified parent' because the enum has no biparental value; both parents carry the variant (homozygous proband). Gene printed only as 'SSADH' (coding sequence/gene) in the variant sentence; reference sequence printed as 'GenBank Y11192' (not an NM transcript), recorded in transcript_as_stated. Parents' variant string recorded as printed ('T/C heterozygotes at position c.667'), no c./p. HGVS fields filled for them; variant type/pathogenicity of the proband's variant not copied to parents. SNP rs2744583 (used only to exclude an exon-4 deletion) not recorded as a variant row. Functional evidence cited is for a different variant at the same codon (c.668G>A), so functional_evidence_statement left not reported. Patient 2: 'enzymatic and molecular confirmation' in white cells but no variant printed, so a variant row with variant_original_string 'not reported' and gene 'not reported'. Patient 2 was previously reported (Crutchfield et al. 2008; Gibson et al. 1988); this citation is copied to source_reference_in_review because her clinical summary is taken from those reports, though the VEP data are first-hand. Patient 2 age at last evaluation not reported: reported at 9 years and VEPs at age 9 years, then 'after a 20-year follow-up' with no age stated. Reference 13 title ('...in a patient without ataxia or convulsions') is not used: the text does not attribute it to patient 2. 'Nerve conduction, electromyography and funduscopy were normal' recorded as excluded abnormal nerve conduction/EMG/funduscopy only (normal investigations as a whole; nothing more specific inferred). Contradictions/tensions: (a) the abstract says binocular VEP latencies were within normal ranges for both patients, but patient 1's binocular latency was 134 ms against an age range of 110-118 ms given for monocular latencies; Results do not call 134 ms abnormal, so only the abstract's excluded statement is recorded. (b) The abstract gives delayed latencies of 134-147 ms, whereas Results give 144 and 150 ms for patient 1 and 147 ms for patient 2 (Discussion: 144-150 ms). (c) Patient 1 amplitudes 1.56 and 9.6 μV are stated as within the lab's normal range (5.6±3.7 μV); recorded as stated. Checklist: 'delayed psychomotor milestones'/'psychomotor delay' not mapped to intellectual disability; 'hyperkinesis' not mapped to attention problems or ADHD; subcortical white-matter T2 hyperintensity not mapped to the globus pallidus/subthalamic/dentate item. Age at onset for patient 1 recorded as 'At birth' (asphyxia, cyanosis, poor cry and sucking at birth).
